LESSON: VOLLEYBALL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.9: Volleyball
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Volleyball, part of Creating and Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: when observing virtual performance of skills. How does the volley pass make the Volleyball game interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Observe virtual or actual performances of a volleyball game and identify the overarm skills of serving the ball. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be adjusted for learners who are sensitive to light

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Observe virtual or actual performances of a volleyball game and identify the overarm skills of serving the ball. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be adjusted for learners who are sensitive to light

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Volleyball together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: the learner collaborates with peers while playing a mini Volleyball game.

● Self-efficacy: Learner develop confidence as they execute the service in Volleyball.

Values:
● Respect: the learner appreciates own and others' performance in executing the arm serve and volleying skills.

● Social justice: the learner respects fellow peers as they demonstrate and practice the service and volleying in Volleyball.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
PCIs:

● Health promotion issues: the learner participates in the physical activities thus acquiring fitness and health.

● Self- awareness: the learner accept their ability in learning new skills in Volleyball.

Link to other learning areas ·

● Integrated Science: the learner connecting theoretical knowledge to practical application in sports as they move different

parts of the body during physical activity.

● Mathematics: executing serving skills involves quick calculations of distances and angles. The learner applies

mathematical concepts to determine the most efficient paths and angles to serve the ball over the net.
